---
title: "Atmospheric deposition and acidity exercises"
---

Use the [notes](notes.qmd). All numerical inputs below are constructed
teaching examples; use the stated assumptions rather than looking up extra
constants. Predict the direction of change before calculating.

## 1. Wet input

Rainfall is 0.600 m/year and nitrate is 20.0 µmol/L throughout. Calculate nitrate input per square metre per year. Use 1 m³ = 1000 L.

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
A metre of rain over one square metre is one cubic metre.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Worked solution"}
600 L/m²/year × 20.0 µmol/L = **0.0120 mol nitrate/m²/year**. This is a nitrate amount flux. Calling it an acid-equivalent flux requires the form and transformations to be specified.
:::

## 2. Rain pH

Two rain events both have pH 4.00 but depths of 1.00 and 10.0 mm. In the dilute approximation, calculate free-H⁺ input per m² for each. Does this include all titratable acidity?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
1 mm over 1 m² is 1 L; [H⁺] = 10⁻⁴ mol/L.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Worked solution"}
Inputs are **0.100 and 1.00 mmol H⁺/m²**. The larger event carries ten times the free hydrogen-ion amount. Other acid–base species and dry deposition are not included.
:::

## 3. Change the catchment budget

Use the worked budget but reduce neutralisation from 30000 to 20000 eq/year. Keep annual water export fixed. Find the residual equivalent load concentration.

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
Subtract equivalents before dividing by the annual volume.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Worked solution"}
Residual = 20000 eq/year. Dividing by 5.00 × 10⁸ L/year gives 4.00 × 10⁻⁵ eq/L = **0.0400 meq/L**. It is not a pH and is not a closed-water pulse.
:::

## 4. A sulfate result

A rain sample contains sulfate. What additional evidence is needed before reporting a strong-acid dose from that result?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
Counterions and subsequent transformations affect acidity.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Worked solution"}
Measure or constrain acidity/alkalinity, major cations including ammonium, other anions, precipitation volume, and dry deposition as relevant. Sulfate may arrive partly as neutral salts. Nitrification, uptake, and catchment reactions can change the net acid budget.
:::

## Explore: deposition and dilution {#explore}

Predict what happens if annual water export doubles while deposition flux and
catchment area stay fixed. Change one input at a time and distinguish flux,
annual load, and the equivalent concentration.

```{=html}
<link rel="stylesheet" href="../demos/demo.css">
<div data-demo="deposition" role="group" aria-label="Deposition, annual load, and dilution">
<p>Reference case: 40000 eq/year of acid input gives 0.0800 meq/L before neutralisation at 500 million L/year water export.</p>
</div>
<script src="../demos/core.js"></script>
<script src="../demos/deposition.js"></script>
```

**E1.** Choose **Worked example**, then **Double water export**. Which annual
amounts stay fixed? Check the equivalent concentration by hand.

**E2.** Reset, then double catchment area while keeping water export fixed.
Explain why this is a different comparison from doubling both area and water.

**E3.** Set both acid inputs to zero. Explain why water volume cannot create
an acid input.

### Model conditions and hand check

The constructed inputs are 20.0 mmol HNO₃ and 10.0 mmol H₂SO₄ per m² per year.
At the stated full-neutralisation endpoint, their equivalent flux is
`(20 + 2 × 10)/1000 = 0.0400 eq/m²/year`. Across 1.00 km² this gives
**40000 eq/year**. Dividing by 500 million L/year gives **0.0800 meq/L**;
doubling that water export gives **0.0400 meq/L** at the same annual load.

These are supplied acid inputs, not sulfate or nitrate measurements treated as
free acid. All input is assumed to reach the annual exported water, with no
storage, neutralisation, or other sinks. This is an annual equivalent budget,
not a closed-lake pulse or a pH prediction. Area and water export are independent
controls only for the stated sensitivity comparison.
